title: The 5 Jobs Every Manager Does | Principles of Management Ep 14
description:
Chai Corner is about to open a second outlet, and Ravi's to-do list is a mess: rent a shop, hire people, buy stoves. He jumps from job to job and finishes nothing. In this animated lesson we use his chai stall to understand the functions of management: the five core jobs every manager does, again and again.

You will see Ravi and his team sort every task into five boxes, then learn where the list comes from: Henri Fayol's five elements (1916) and Luther Gulick's POSDCORB (1937). Each function answers one question at Chai Corner: planning, organizing, staffing, directing and controlling. We plan the 14-day opening and watch coordination remove three idle days, see Meena open the bus stand outlet with two new helpers, and run the cycle: week one falls short, controlling sends Ravi back to planning, and week four beats the goal. We also see the five at work in schools, hospitals, airlines, cricket teams and delivery apps, and look honestly at the limits: Henry Mintzberg (1973) found that real managers jump between short tasks all day.

This is Episode 14 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
